findings.description: Round-2 /metrics Prometheus exposition injection is closed. The route label is now the matched route template (not the raw percent-decoded path) and _escape_label escapes backslash, double-quote and newline. Verified: the round-2 vector GET /%22%7D...%0A produced a 404 into the bounded <unmatched> series, no forged http_requests_total series appeared, and slo-check.js reports pass / 0% error against 1% budget. Residual (INFO, defence-in-depth): _LABEL_ESCAPES omits carriage return and the other C0 control characters, but no reachable channel delivers them - method is filtered by the httptools/llhttp parser (a method containing CR, quote or backslash yields 400 before the counter runs), route comes only from source-code templates, and status is an int.
findings.fix: Escape or reject all C0 control characters (including \r) in _escape_label so the control is robust if a channel ever carries raw bytes.

findings.description: Round-2 unbounded /metrics cardinality is closed. Measured: 1500 requests to distinct unmatched paths collapsed into a single route="<unmatched>" series; the counter series count stayed at 8 and the duration count series stayed at 8. The new histogram dicts _duration_counts / _duration_totals key on (method, route_label(scope)) and inherit the same route bound. The method component does not re-open growth: httptools/llhttp rejects unknown method tokens with 400 (FOOBAR, GET_PARAMETER -> 400), so method is confined to the parser's fixed method table.
findings.fix: None required. Optionally cap the number of distinct method labels defensively in case of a future parser swap.

findings.description: Round-2 SEC-103 (int/bool values and mapping KEYS bypassed scrub_text) is closed by f5a5ace. Verified with live values under an open redaction scope: sanitise_context({'uid': 234123412346}) -> {'uid': '[REDACTED]'}; a 12-digit Aadhaar used as a KEY -> {'[REDACTED]': 'x'}; 'pan-ABCDE1234F' as a key -> {'pan-[REDACTED]': 'ok'}; string PAN value -> '[REDACTED]'. Harmless bools still pass through as bool.

Redaction is defeated by trivial reformatting. Verified with live scrub_text under a scope registering PAN ABCDE1234F and Aadhaar 234123412346: dot-, underscore- and slash-separated forms, NBSP (U+00A0), zero-width (U+200B) and fullwidth-digit variants all LEAK unredacted; only exact, lowercase, <=4-run space/dash forms are caught. This is currently latent, not exploitable: grep confirms ZERO production call sites of register_sensitive / redact_values in backend/src (commit ba457bf added the call sites only to the specs for E4-S1 and E1-S1, whose handlers do not exist in group A). Escalates to a data-exposure BLOCK the moment POST /applications or POST /auth/login is implemented and registers real PAN/Aadhaar/password values.
findings.fix: Normalize-then-match: NFKC-normalize and strip zero-width/formatting characters from both the value and the haystack before matching, rather than only tolerating a bounded space/dash run. Add the fix before E4-S1/E1-S1 land.

findings.description: _redaction_pattern is @lru_cache(maxsize=256) keyed on the raw sensitive value, so up to 256 PAN/Aadhaar/password strings are retained verbatim in process memory for the lifetime of the process, well beyond the request scope the redaction set otherwise enforces. Latent while there are no register_sensitive call sites; becomes a real retention/exposure issue once handlers register PII.
findings.fix: Cache on a non-sensitive derived key (e.g. a structural signature) or drop the lru_cache and compile per-scope; never hold PII as a cache key.

findings.description: Inbound X-Request-ID is accepted unvalidated and unbounded (a 16 KB value was accepted, echoed verbatim on the response and logged verbatim in the request_id JSON field; larger values are only rejected by the parser's header-size limit). No CRLF / log-line injection is possible - the parser rejects CR/LF in the header value and JSONLogFormatter serialises request_id through json.dumps which escapes control characters - but an arbitrary attacker-chosen id enters logs and the response, enabling log-bloat and correlation-id spoofing, and any PII a client places in the header is logged unredacted.
findings.fix: Validate X-Request-ID against a bounded charset/length (e.g. <=128 chars, [A-Za-z0-9._-]) and generate a fresh id when it fails.

findings.description: Starlette redirect_slashes is left on. GET /health/ with Host: evil.example returns 307 with Location: http://evil.example/health - the redirect target reflects the attacker-controlled Host header. Behind a proxy that forwards an arbitrary Host this is a host-header-reflected open redirect / cache-poisoning primitive.
findings.fix: Disable redirect_slashes (FastAPI(redirect_slashes=False)) or build redirect Location from a configured canonical host, never from the request Host header.

findings.description: No security response headers are set on any route. Verified GET /health returns no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or Strict-Transport-Security.
findings.fix: Add a response-header middleware setting at least X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors), and HSTS when served over TLS.

findings.description: Money.format() thousands-separator regex /\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g is quadratic in the integer-digit count. Measured in node: 20k digits = 157 ms, 50k digits = 1008 ms (O(n^2)). No upstream bound caps the magnitude of a Money reaching format(), so a crafted/oversized amount from an API response or user input freezes the browser tab (client-side DoS). Untouched by every round-3 remediation commit.
findings.fix: Bound the integer length before formatting (money amounts have a sane maximum), or replace the lookahead grouping with a linear pass / Intl.NumberFormat.

findings.description: /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json are publicly reachable (all 200). For group A the documented surface is only /health and /metrics, so disclosure is minimal now, but this should be gated before the origination/auth routes ship.
findings.fix: Disable the interactive docs in production or place them behind auth once group B/E routes are added.

findings.description: /metrics is unauthenticated. Deferral is deliberate and documented (E15-S4 Scope Out: auth needs an api-contracts.md amendment plus the auth layer arriving with E1-S1 in group B). Judged defensible: the endpoint exposes only bounded RED counters and a latency histogram (method/route-template/status counts) with no PII, secrets or attacker-injectable series, so unauthenticated read is low-risk operational disclosure.
findings.fix: Honour the E15-S4 Scope Out commitment to gate /metrics when the auth layer lands with E1-S1.

findings.description: HEAD /health returns 405 (no HEAD handler registered). Not a security issue; noted for probe/monitoring compatibility.
findings.fix: Allow HEAD on /health if load balancers probe with HEAD.
